newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-MIAMI AND CHICAGO TO JOIN MLS IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIAMI AND CHICAGO TO JOIN MLS IN 1998.

text.p: Major League Soccer will add teams in Miami and Chicago for the 1998 season, expanding the league to 12 teams, MLS Commissioner Douglas Logan announced on Wednesday.
"We are pleased to announce that Miami and Chicago will join Major League Soccer in 1998," Logan said.
The Miami franchise will play its home games at the Orange Bowl, while the Chicago club will be based at Soldier Field, home to the National Football League's Chicago Bears.
Chicago, home of the U.S. Soccer Federation, has been the largest market in the United States without a MLS team.

Logan said the league had reached an agreement on a 10-year lease for the Orange Bowl and a five-year lease for the use of Soldier Field. Formal agreements on both leases are expected by July 1, Logan said.
Chicago had been chosen as one of the 10 initial sites for MLS teams, but the franchise was shifted to Dallas after an impasse with the group that runs Soldier Field.
The Miami team will be operated by a group headed by Kenneth Horowitz, a Florida-based communications entrepreneur.
The league accepted an offer of $20 million from the Horowitz group for the Miami franchise, Logan said in a statement issued by MLS.
The large Latin American population of south Florida makes Miami a natural site for a soccer club.
Anchutz Chicago Soccer Inc. will run the Chicago club. Philip Anchutz already owns the MLS Colorado Rapids and the National Hockey League's Los Angeles Kings.
In its inaugural season last year, MLS averaged 17,416 fans for each of its 160 games played.
